virals.hook: It's been a while since the last recap, had a few things keeping me occupied but we're back with another round
virals.text:
It's been a while since the last recap, had a few things keeping me occupied but we're back with another roundup, let's get into it...

here are nine developments worth catching up on

1. OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber

GPT-6 Cyber just went live and it is a specialised model designed to help cybersecurity researchers identify software vulnerabilities and understand how they could be exploited and develop fixes

It received a Critical rating under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework and scored 48.5% on the ExploitGym vulnerability exploitation benchmark

Access is initially limited to selected members of its Daybreak Red programme for authorised defensive security work

2. Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro open weights

Moonshot AI has released the weights for Kimi K3.1 Pro, allowing developers to download and run the model themselves. First introduced in October, the weights became available on November 4

The multimodal model has 2.8 trillion total parameters, 104 billion active parameters and a context window of around one million tokens

3. OpenAI launches Images 2.6

OpenAI introduced Images 2.6, bringing faster image generation, more consistent editing and better control over visual details

It's reportedly 50% faster than the previous version and now supports GIF generation

4. Anthropic releases FlashProve

Anthropic introduced FlashProve, an opensource system that helps verify whether an AI response actually came from the model a provider claims to be using

It uses cryptographic proofs without exposing the model's internal weights

5. Sarvam AI releases Prism

Indian AI company Sarvam AI introduced Prism, an openweight model built for fast decision making rather than generating long responses

Based on Sarvam 105B, it evaluates options and assigns probabilities to them

6. Meituan releases LongCat-2.5

Meituan introduced @Meituan_LongCat, a multimodal model designed to handle long-running AI agent tasks

It has 1.6 trillion total parameters, with 48 billion active per token. It's built for tasks ranging from complex coding and software development to creative design and 3D work

7. Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor

Meta has acquired Conductor, a startup that helps developers run multiple AI coding agents in parallel and manage their work from one interface

8. Anthropic updates Claude's restrictions on video game creation

Anthropic has updated Claude Code's instructions to discourage it from recreating existing copyrighted video games

Claude can still help developers build original games, work within specific genres and create games using their own designs and assets

The change aims to prevent direct copying of existing games without restricting legitimate game development

9. OpenAI pipeline generates 948 Linux exploits

OpenAI revealed that its AI powered security pipeline generated 948 working exploits targeting the Linux kernel

The system examined 2,308 potential security issues, reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities and developed candidate patches. 

The process cost approximately $1.21 million in API credits, with human researchers still needed to review the findings and proposed fixes

that's all for now, talk soon

outsiders.name: Precyblazer
outsiders.hook: It's been a while since the last recap, had a few things keeping me occupied but we're back with another round
outsiders.text:
It's been a while since the last recap, had a few things keeping me occupied but we're back with another roundup, let's get into it...

here are nine developments worth catching up on

1. OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber

GPT-6 Cyber just went live and it is a specialised model designed to help cybersecurity researchers identify software vulnerabilities and understand how they could be exploited and develop fixes

It received a Critical rating under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework and scored 48.5% on the ExploitGym vulnerability exploitation benchmark

Access is initially limited to selected members of its Daybreak Red programme for authorised defensive security work

2. Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro open weights

Moonshot AI has released the weights for Kimi K3.1 Pro, allowing developers to download and run the model themselves. First introduced in October, the weights became available on November 4

The multimodal model has 2.8 trillion total parameters, 104 billion active parameters and a context window of around one million tokens

3. OpenAI launches Images 2.6

OpenAI introduced Images 2.6, bringing faster image generation, more consistent editing and better control over visual details

It's reportedly 50% faster than the previous version and now supports GIF generation

4. Anthropic releases FlashProve

Anthropic introduced FlashProve, an opensource system that helps verify whether an AI response actually came from the model a provider claims to be using

It uses cryptographic proofs without exposing the model's internal weights

5. Sarvam AI releases Prism

Indian AI company Sarvam AI introduced Prism, an openweight model built for fast decision making rather than generating long responses

Based on Sarvam 105B, it evaluates options and assigns probabilities to them

6. Meituan releases LongCat-2.5

Meituan introduced @Meituan_LongCat, a multimodal model designed to handle long-running AI agent tasks

It has 1.6 trillion total parameters, with 48 billion active per token. It's built for tasks ranging from complex coding and software development to creative design and 3D work

7. Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor

Meta has acquired Conductor, a startup that helps developers run multiple AI coding agents in parallel and manage their work from one interface

8. Anthropic updates Claude's restrictions on video game creation

Anthropic has updated Claude Code's instructions to discourage it from recreating existing copyrighted video games

Claude can still help developers build original games, work within specific genres and create games using their own designs and assets

The change aims to prevent direct copying of existing games without restricting legitimate game development

9. OpenAI pipeline generates 948 Linux exploits

OpenAI revealed that its AI powered security pipeline generated 948 working exploits targeting the Linux kernel

The system examined 2,308 potential security issues, reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities and developed candidate patches. 

The process cost approximately $1.21 million in API credits, with human researchers still needed to review the findings and proposed fixes

that's all for now, talk soon
